C50.content_en:
Ways to see how the top results change — and how the main tools compare

If you aim for a top spot with an affiliate article, you want to know whether the top results for a keyword are fixed or rotating. Enter a keyword and this tool shows the top 10 results of the past year at each point in time that was captured, as rank and domain.

Method / toolPricing modelNotes
This tool (DataForSEO)Pay per request. About $0.0007 per call (measured for "how to start a blog"; may vary with the number of snapshots)One keyword's past top-10 results by snapshot in a table. Save as CSV
Ahrefs Keywords Explorer (SERP overview)Subscription (see the official site for plans)Has a SERP overview view (see the official site for whether history is included)
Recording it yourself every day (by hand)FreeNote the top sites yourself and it becomes a history. You cannot go back in time
Looking at today's results (by hand)FreeYou see today's top sites, not past ones

Checked in November 2026. Prices change — confirm on each vendor's official site before you buy.

Why use this tool

  • Look back in time. See about a year of line-ups even if you never recorded them.
  • About $0.0007 per call. About 1,400 per $1, so you can try many keywords.
  • See whether #1 changes. For "how to start a blog", #1 was theblogstarter.com in two of the three saved snapshots and reddit.com in the other, while the rest rotated (measured).
  • A few seconds at most. The sample call took under a second (measured).
  • Save as CSV.

When it is not the right fit

  • You want a monthly trend → results come at the captured moments, not monthly. The saved sample for "how to start a blog" shows three: Dec 2025, Jul 2026 and Nov 2026 (measured).
  • You want rank 11 and below → only the top 10 per snapshot are shown; each stored SERP holds about 100 results, but the table omits them.
  • You want other result blocks (AI overviews, related questions, video) → only organic results are shown.
  • You want daily changes → snapshots are months apart.
  • The same domain can appear several times within one snapshot's top 10 (different pages). We show them as they come.

This tool does one thing: show a keyword's top-10 results over the past year, snapshot by snapshot.

FAQ

Why is it not monthly?

The API's history only holds the moments it captured. The number and spacing of snapshots may differ by keyword.

Why only the top 10?

To serve as a "who is on top" tool, we limit it to the top 10. That limit is this tool's own rule.

How much does it cost?

About $0.0007 for the sample call ("how to start a blog"); it may vary a little with the number of snapshots.

What do country and language change?

The market for the numbers. For example, the United States and English give the history of US results.

Can I sign up with a free email address?

No. DataForSEO does not accept free email providers. See What is DataForSEO?

C51.content_en:
Ways to see a site's estimated traffic trend — and how the main tools compare

When you manage or promote a company, you want to check whether your site's search traffic is growing. Enter a domain and this tool shows the last 12 months of estimated traffic and keyword count, month by month.

Method / toolPricing modelNotes
This tool (DataForSEO)Pay per request. About $0.136 per call for 12 months (measured)A domain's past 12 months of estimated traffic and keyword count in a table. Works on other people's sites. Save as CSV
Google Search ConsoleFreeShows your own site's real search impressions and clicks. You cannot view other sites
Ahrefs Site Explorer (Overview)Subscription (see the official site for plans)Shows a site's search traffic trend and more. The free version covers only sites you verify (per Ahrefs' page)
SimilarwebSubscription (its pricing page lists a Starter plan from $125/month)A service that estimates site traffic trends and more (see the official site for features)

Checked in November 2026. Prices change — confirm on each vendor's official site before you buy.

Why use this tool

  • A monthly trend in a table. target.com showed about 72.3 million in December 2025 and about 52.4 million in October 2026 (measured).
  • About $0.136 for 12 months. Higher per call than other tools, but you get a full year at once.
  • Works on other people's sites. See a rival's momentum too.
  • A few seconds. The sample call took about 3.6 seconds (measured).
  • Save as CSV. Make your own chart.

When it is not the right fit

  • You want to test cheaply and often → at about $0.136 per call this is on the high side for this series.
  • You want real visit counts → estimated traffic is a modeled figure from rankings and search volume (per DataForSEO), not real visitors.
  • You read the whole series as a drop → for target.com, estimated traffic fell from about 64.6 million (November 2025) to about 52.4 million (October 2026) over the 12 months, and keywords from about 14.7 million to about 8.5 million (measured); the peak was about 76.9 million in April 2026. Check against other measures before drawing conclusions.
  • You want this month's figure → the current month is partial and comes out small, so it is left out of the table. The table shows the last 12 complete months.
  • You want more than 12 months → the tool stops at 12.

This tool does one thing: show a domain's monthly estimated traffic and keyword count for the past 12 months.

FAQ

Why is one call so expensive?

The API's price per call is high. It does not scale with the months: the sample call for target.com (13 months fetched, 12 shown) cost $0.1356, and an earlier Japan test with six months cost $0.127 (measured in Japan).

Which 12 months?

The twelve months ending with the month you run it. The start date is set automatically from today.

Why is this month missing from the table?

A month in progress shows a small figure, so the tool drops it and shows the last 12 complete months. It fetches 13 months and removes the current one.

What do country and language change?

The market for the numbers. For example, the United States and English give numbers for US results.

Can I sign up with a free email address?

No. DataForSEO does not accept free email providers. See What is DataForSEO?
